What is the legal gambling age in Canada?
19 in most provinces and territories, and 18 in Quebec, Alberta and Manitoba. The age applies online and in land-based casinos, and every casino on this page checks ID before it pays out.
How do I tell licensed casinos from unlicensed ones?
Take the licence number from the footer or terms and look it up on the regulator’s own register, not on a seal or a third-party site. Check that the register names the same company and, where it lists them, the same domain you are playing on. The licence table on this page shows what each register showed for the casinos we list.
Is it safe to play at offshore online casinos?
It can be, if you check three things first: the licence appears on the issuing regulator’s own register under the same company and domain, the terms name a complaints route, and a small first withdrawal arrives as promised. What you give up offshore is provincial protection, because disputes go to the regulator abroad and provincial self-exclusion does not reach these sites.
Which online casino actually pays out real money?
Every casino we tested paid out. In our July 2026 round, all 16 timed withdrawals across eight casinos arrived, from 7 h 30 min to 48 h 20 min after the request, and the later round on this page completed four first-deposit withdrawals with none rejected. Payout speed depends mostly on verification, so upload your documents on the day you register.
Do any casinos in Canada offer free spins without a deposit?
None of the casinos on this page runs a standing no deposit bonus or no deposit free spins, and third-party codes promising one for these brands are usually out of date. Free spins here come with a deposit, from 300 to 500 on the bigger welcome packages, so judge them by the wagering on spin winnings and how fast they expire.
